sources.entry: numactl - Reference implementation of the policy API, prints the distance table and binds a binary that cannot be rebuilt.

summary.one_liner: numactl is a Linux tool and C library for setting NUMA memory placement policy, both for running programs under a given policy and for applications calling the libnuma API.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a numactl program that runs other programs under a specific NUMA policy, and a libnuma shared library (the "NUMA API") that applications can use to set NUMA policy themselves. The README says the libnuma binary interface is meant to stay binary compatible, with incompatible changes using new symbol version numbers. It also ships utility programs such as numastat, which displays NUMA allocation statistics, and memhog. A small regression test suite lives in the test/ directory. The README says the regression test assumes an unloaded machine with free memory on each node, otherwise the non-strict policies (preferred, interleave) may show spurious failures. Manpages numactl.8 and numa.3 document usage.
use_cases: run a program with interleaved memory across NUMA nodes
bind a process to specific NUMA nodes
view NUMA allocation statistics with numastat
set NUMA memory policy from a C application via libnuma
test NUMA policy behavior with the regression suite
benchmark memory bandwidth per NUMA node with numademo
stack: GNU General Public License v2 programs
notable: Ships both a command-line policy launcher (numactl) and a C library (libnuma) for applications
Includes numastat for NUMA allocation statistics and memhog for memory load testing
Includes numademo, which bundles a derived STREAM benchmark sub-test
Binary compatibility policy for libnuma using symbol versioning
caveats: The regression suite assumes an unloaded machine with free memory on each node; otherwise non-strict policy tests can fail spuriously
Publishing numademo output may require attention to STREAM benchmark licensing; the STREAM results may need filtering
